previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old female was admitted after an intentional overdose of 20 morphine tablets in the context of severe major depression, chronic abdominal pain from endometriosis, and opiate abuse. She had a history of prior unintentional acetaminophen overdose causing liver injury and pancreatitis, recent breakup, legal issues, and substance use. Initially tearful and depressed, she gradually improved with mirtazapine and quetiapine, discontinued lorazepam, and successfully tapered off narcotics using gabapentin, lidocaine patch, and ibuprofen. A urinary tract infection was treated with Augmentin and resolved. She gained insight into her coping mechanisms, engaged in therapy, and planned to attend a partial hospitalization program. By discharge, her mood was stable, pain was controlled, and she denied suicidal ideation. She was discharged home with her mother, on a regimen of mirtazapine, quetiapine, gabapentin, and other maintenance medications, with follow-up planned.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, severe, without mention of psychotic behavior
Urinary tract infection, site not specified

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year-old woman with extensive past 
psychiatric history and repeated suicide attempts who presented 
from the ___ inpatient ___ facility with confusion and 
progressive lethargy in the setting of uptitrated psychiatric 
medications. 

Hospital Course
---------------
The patient was transferred from ___ to the ___ ED due to 
confusion and increasing lethargy. On arrival at ___ she was 
noted to have mydriasis on exam and was lethargic. CT head did 
not show any acute process and CXR was also unremarkable. The 
patient was admitted to the general medicine floor. On the 
floor, the patient was noted to have psychiatric medication 
polypharmacy causing toxic encephalopathy.  This was thought to 
be the etiology of her lethargy. She was continued only on 
Klonipin and lamotrigine and her mental status began to improve. 
The patient was seen by psychiatry on HOD #1 and agreed with 
this management. A ___ was in the chart. 

Throughout the ___ hospital stay she continuously 
described various types of head pain that did not respond to 
NSAIDs. She repeatedly asked for narcotics however these were 
not provided. On ___, it appeared the patient had a migraine 
type headache and she was given fioronal 
(Aspirin-Caffeine-Butalbital) that helped relieve the symptoms. 
The patient had no further HA pain. The following day she 
complained of diarrhea. A C. Diff toxin assay was negative. This 
symptoms also resolved without further intervention.

Psychiatry agreed that the patient would require continued 
inpatient psychiatric care once medically cleared and she was 
declared medically clear on ___. Intermittently during her 
stay while awaiting a psychiatric bed, she would become agitated 
and required 1 dose of IM haldol during on occurrance from which 
she could not be talked down.

She also intermittently complainted of various physical ailments 
none of which ever bore out an underling physiologic cause when 
evaluated by physicians. It was thought these symptomatic 
complaints were either a means of gaining attention or an 
attempt to get pain medications or other sedating/anxiety 
suppressing medications. She has some history of narcotic abuse.

Chronic Conditions
------------------
#. Migraine headaches - The patient had migraine headaches while 
inpatient here. Treated with fioronal. Was previously on 
verapamil for prophylaxis although had borderline/low BPs so 
this was not continued. 

#. Asthma: Stable. Continued Advair and albuterol PRN.

#. GERD: Stable. Continued omeprazole.
  
#. Hypothyroidism: TSH slightly elevated at just >5 per Arbour 
records and patient started on levothyroxine. This was 
discontinued here at it was unclear what setting the patient's 
TSH was elevated in. Should be evaluated further on an 
outpatient basis.
